solution: M3 / 2015 root definitions: sqrt(81) denotes the nonnegative square root of 81, so sqrt(81)=9. Thus a^2=9 has exactly the two real roots -3 and 3; a<0 selects a=-3. The equation a+b=7 then forces b=10, which satisfies b>0. Hence N=b^2=100>0. Conversely, (a,b,N)=(-3,10,100) satisfies every stated condition, proving existence. Each variable was forced in order, proving uniqueness over the full real domain, not merely among the options. For N=16,49,81,100,256 respectively, b>0 forces b=4,7,9,10,16; with a=-3 the sums are 1,4,6,7,13. Only the fourth option satisfies a+b=7. No lengths, units, or figure conditions are stated; the positive domains of b and N are satisfied. Answer: ④ ($100$).
